concepts.title: What Makes Creative Reusable?
concepts.viewerQuestion: What turns a one-time AI output into a creative system another agent can repeat?
concepts.viewerLearns: Prompts request outputs, while Formats preserve the instructions, judgment, and proof needed to repeat them.
concepts.whyInteresting: It explains a difference most people using generative AI have never named.
concepts.whyNotAnAd: The lesson compares familiar creative building blocks instead of listing Wiggly features or asking the viewer to buy.
concepts.finalTakeaway: Wiggly makes the whole creative system reusable.

concepts.title: Why One Good Output Is Not a Format
concepts.viewerQuestion: What is missing when AI makes one strong creative but cannot reliably make the next one?
concepts.viewerLearns: Repeatability requires preserved rules, examples, and quality checks rather than another isolated prompt.
concepts.whyInteresting: It starts from the common frustration of getting one lucky result that cannot be reproduced.
concepts.whyNotAnAd: It teaches why reproducibility is difficult without making product promises.
concepts.finalTakeaway: A reusable format turns one lucky result into a repeatable creative system.

concepts.title: Tools Do Not Make the Creative Decision
concepts.viewerQuestion: What is the difference between connecting AI tools and directing good creative?
concepts.viewerLearns: Execution tools move media, while creative instructions decide what should happen and whether it worked.
concepts.whyInteresting: It reveals the missing layer inside many visual AI workflows.
concepts.whyNotAnAd: The concept explains a technical distinction instead of presenting a sales claim.
concepts.finalTakeaway: The tools execute the workflow, but the skill preserves the creative judgment.

concepts.title: A Reference Is Not a Recipe
concepts.viewerQuestion: Why can an agent see a great example and still fail to recreate what makes it work?
concepts.viewerLearns: Examples show the result, while a Format also explains the structure, assets, process, and acceptance criteria.
concepts.whyInteresting: It explains why visual imitation often misses the original format's real grammar.
concepts.whyNotAnAd: The story focuses on a creative-production problem rather than promoting a feature list.
concepts.finalTakeaway: A runnable kit turns inspiration into a process another agent can repeat.

concepts.title: Where Creative Knowledge Goes
concepts.viewerQuestion: What happens when a working creative process exists only in one person's memory?
concepts.viewerLearns: Packaging the process lets another agent operate it without hidden context.
concepts.whyInteresting: It turns an invisible handoff problem into something concrete.
concepts.whyNotAnAd: The lesson is about transferring creative knowledge, not purchasing software.
concepts.finalTakeaway: Packaging the process turns one creator's memory into a skill any agent can run.
